A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the layout and section changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning results, retrieval-head correlations, masking and patching experiments, and all-module LoRA analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix analyses, and adds patching results and statistical significance reporting.

M1.justification: The synthetic-data construction procedures, attention-only LoRA training, retrieval-head detection, and activation patching procedures remain unchanged. The all-module LoRA configuration was already evaluated in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use MDQA, linear three-hop MuSiQue, and SummHay Citation, with the same synthetic, symbolic, and limited-relation variants. The added patching row uses an existing MuSiQue data condition.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same synthetic-data, real-data, and non-fine-tuned comparisons. Patching comparisons retain complement, intersection, random-head, and original-model conditions; the added row introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: The models, 8K-to-32K context extension, training sample counts, 90/10 splits, greedy decoding, and patching selection rule remain unchanged. The additional significance tests do not change the reported evaluation design.

E4.justification: Table 3 extends the existing head-patching analysis to Llama-3 on MuSiQue with low concept expression and high context diversity. The masking experiment and all-module LoRA analyses are retained, with masking relocated to Appendix F.

E5.justification: v3 introduces paired-bootstrap significance testing at p < 0.05 for central synthetic-data comparisons in Table 1 and patching effects in Tables 3 and 11. This adds inferential support absent from v2 across two principal experimental analyses. The three random-mask trials remain unchanged; additional training runs are not documented.

E6.justification: The new MuSiQue low-expression/high-diversity row in Table 3 reports patching 58 heads: complement F1 0.37, intersection 0.19, and random 0.27, against original F1 0.29. Retained F1 values are unchanged. Tables 3 and 11 remove their explicit improvement columns while retaining the underlying scores.

T1.justification: The formal setup, retrieval and insight score definitions in Equations 1–2, and patching-set definitions remain equivalent. No theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the first contribution from determining best practices to characterizing effects of data realism, and frames the second more specifically around retrieval-score correlations. The central conclusion that retrieval heads are necessary but insufficient remains.

C2.justification: v3 removes v2 Section 5's interpretation linking stronger intersection-head scores to a distinction between core and dynamically activated retrieval heads, although Table 12 retains the evidence. The representation-shift explanation and necessary-but-insufficient qualification remain.

D1.justification: v3 omits the Reproducibility statement promising data-generation, training, and analysis scripts, and the explicit description of masking by zeroing head outputs. Prompts, LoRA settings, hardware, and Baukit patching instructions remain. Actual withdrawal of available code is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds An et al. (2024), Wang et al. (2024), and Veličković et al. (2024), expanding discussion of realistic context-extension data and softmax limitations. Updated publication references for existing works, including Wu and Xiong, are not new research additions.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive localized rewrites. Retrieval-head analyses are reorganized, with former Section 5 becoming Section 4.5 and masking moving to Appendix F. Reproducibility is removed and an Impact Statement added; most remaining prose is retained.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint main text becomes a two-column conference layout, broadly changing figure and table sizing and placement. Masking Figure 3 becomes appendix Figure 9, the correlation plot is redrawn, and Tables 3 and 11 receive revised columns, highlighting, and significance legends.

improvement.justification: The added bootstrap tests make central empirical comparisons easier to assess, and the additional patching condition improves completeness. More focused contribution wording also helps. These are limited gains because the underlying study and most results remain unchanged; removing the script-release commitment and some procedural detail modestly reduces reproducibility information.
